title: Refusing to see him
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on a psychiatric ward. Mr Hale, 45, who has a previous conviction for a sexual offence, has developed a high temperature and needs a physical health review.

Your F2 colleague, who is on call for the ward, says, "I'm not seeing him after what he's done," and asks you to do it instead.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 4 = Least appropriate).

options.brief: A senior should know, particularly if it continues.
options.detailed: The consultant may need to address it, especially if it affects care. It ranks third because a direct conversation should come first.

options.text: See Mr Hale yourself so his care isn't delayed.
options.brief: His physical health needs attention now.
options.detailed: He has a fever and needs assessment. Making sure he is seen promptly comes first, whatever the disagreement between colleagues. It ranks first.

options.text: Talk with your colleague privately about her refusal.
options.brief: Her reasons may matter, and the principle needs discussing.
options.detailed: Doctors mustn't refuse to treat patients because of their past. But she may have a personal reason that deserves sensitivity. A private conversation addresses both. It ranks second.

options.text: Agree that she doesn't have to see him.
options.detailed: This accepts her refusal without challenge and may affect his future care. It is the least appropriate option.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you make sure a patient gets care, and challenge a colleague's refusal to treat him because of his past.
explanation.keyDetails: He needs a physical review now. Your colleague refuses because of his conviction. She may have personal reasons.
explanation.reasoning: [B] makes sure he is seen, [C] addresses it with your colleague, and [A] involves a senior. [D] accepts discrimination.
explanation.competing: Some would talk to your colleague first. The key puts his care first because he is unwell, and the conversation can follow.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 2, not refusing or delaying treatment because of a patient's background or past.

references.title: Personal beliefs and medical practice
references.note: Personal beliefs must not lead to unfair treatment of patients.
